FISHING LICENCE · UNITED STATES

Delaware fishing licence

Visitors aged 16 or older need a licence for fresh and tidal waters. A licence exemption does not always remove the separate FIN registration requirement.

Buy a licence online ↗Official rules ↗

Updated 2026-11-11

Who needs one

  • Non-residents aged 16 or older.
  • Recreational fish, crab, and clam harvesters, unless exempt.

Who doesn’t

  • Children under 16 need no general fishing licence.
  • Resident seniors have an exemption that does not extend to visiting seniors.

Licence options and prices

LicenceForLengthPrice
Non-resident annualnon residentAnnual$20 USD
Non-resident 7-daynon resident7 consecutive days$12.50 USD

Extra stamps and permits

  • Fisherman Information Network number · $0 USD
    Required registration; issued with most individual fishing licences.
  • Non-resident trout stamp · $6.20 USD
    Required from age 12 in designated trout streams during the stated spring and autumn periods.

Saltwater

One general licence covers fresh and tidal waters, including recreational crabs and clams.

Rules visitors should know

  • A non-resident boat licence does not cover fishing from shore.
  • The surf-vehicle permit exemption covers the vehicle operator, not every passenger.

How to buy

Use Digital DNREC, authorised licence agents, or the DNREC licensing desk in Dover. Agent fees can apply.

Common license questions

Do I need a fishing licence in Delaware?

Visitors aged 16 or older need a licence for fresh and tidal waters. A licence exemption does not always remove the separate FIN registration requirement.

How much is a visitor fishing licence in Delaware?

Non-resident annual: $20 USD; Non-resident 7-day: $12.50 USD (checked November 2026).

Where do I buy a fishing licence in Delaware?

Use Digital DNREC, authorised licence agents, or the DNREC licensing desk in Dover. Agent fees can apply.
